Pet Travel Basics for Aurelia Skyways

Traveling with a companion animal is usually straightforward when you plan a little ahead and keep to the normal airport flow. At the Companion Animal Travel Desk, we focus on simple steps that reduce stress for you and your pet, from check-in through arrival. If you are moving with a carrier, a leash, or comfort items, keep everything close and easy to reach.

Before you head to the airport, make sure the carrier is secure, the bedding is familiar, and any required documents are packed in an outer pocket. A safety coordinator reviews hazards and prevention before the animal moves through the system, and that helps the day stay calm and predictable. If your pet tends to settle better with routine, keep feeding and exercise as close to normal as possible.

At the terminal, follow signs for the pet areas and ask staff for the smoothest path if your pet needs a rest break. <<FACT F016>> Use the relief area only as directed, then return to the main flow so your journey stays on track. A ground team moves carriers carefully between services, so handoffs stay steady and controlled.

During boarding and the flight itself, the cabin team monitors animals and keeps an eye on comfort and ventilation. You should keep carriers closed unless staff tell you otherwise, and avoid adding loose items that could shift around. If your pet is nervous, speak softly and move slowly, since calm behavior from the traveler often helps the animal settle.

If you are connecting through another station, keep your documents, carrier, and contact details with you at all times. <<FACT F001>> Follow the guidance offered at the desk, since local arrangements can differ from one station to another. That way, your trip stays organized without extra surprises.

If anything changes, check back with the Companion Animal Travel Desk for the latest handling guidance and live support.
